# Planearby

> A personal nearby-aircraft dashboard built with Vue 3. Korean, English, and Japanese interfaces are available.

Planearby starts a scan automatically when the page opens and requests browser location permission when needed. It displays aircraft within a horizontal great-circle distance of the configured radius, excluding altitude (currently 25 km). Each scan ends within 30 seconds and refreshes positions every 7 seconds. Only supported Airbus, Boeing and Bombardier types are displayed; GLEX, helicopters, other manufacturers and unknown types are excluded. The radar plots distance and bearing relative to a manually selected facing direction or an explicitly enabled phone compass. Aircraft noses show reported ground track relative to that facing direction. Phone sensor headings are approximate and may be magnetic rather than true north.

An analog split-flap board shows one selected aircraft. It starts with the closest aircraft and rotates to an unseen aircraft every 10 seconds. Users can select an aircraft on the radar or pause automatic rotation. Reduced-motion preferences disable the flap animation. Flight details are fetched only for selected aircraft and reused within each scan.

Fictional example flights are available only through an explicitly selected example view. These are not live observations. Empty results do not prove there are no aircraft nearby: type filtering, receiver coverage and data delay affect results.

Position source: adsb.lol, licensed under ODbL 1.0. Without an API key, adsbdb supplies origin and destination airports as reference routes matched by callsign. They are not verified as today's flight and do not include scheduled times. The interface marks these limitations and does not estimate schedules. Optional AirLabs details require a server-side API key and a verified match to the observed aircraft. If available, scheduled times are local to each departure or arrival airport, not actual or estimated times.

Exact user coordinates are not written to persistent storage. The server keeps scan coordinates in memory for at most 30 seconds. Theme and language preferences are stored locally in the browser. The interface is for curiosity and is not a navigation or safety tool.

- [adsb.lol API](https://api.adsb.lol/docs)
- [adsb.lol license](https://www.adsb.lol/docs/open-data/api/)
- [adsbdb API fields](https://github.com/mrjackwills/adsbdb)
- [AirLabs flight fields](https://airlabs.co/docs/flight)

Airline identity: verified API airline codes take precedence. If missing, an ICAO or IATA flight-number prefix is matched against a generated OpenFlights airline snapshot. Names and IATA/ICAO pairs are not maintained in a handwritten map. Registration-only and ambiguous codes are not guessed. Callsign-derived names are inferred, not confirmation of the actual operator. OpenFlights data is licensed under ODbL 1.0: https://openflights.org/data.php#airline.
